mathematical_parameters: old value w:Int, new value v:Int
invariant: Forall j in [0,i): select(A,n+j)=v AND Forall j in [i,L): select(A,n+j)=w.
inductive_lemmas: Stage0 starts at i=0: prefix value condition vacuous for ANY original array, assuming n,L>0.
Next-stage initialization: all elements of previous full array [0,L) equal w implies invariant at i=0 for arbitrary v.
Atomic store: invariant at 0≤i<L and store(A,n+i,v), i'=i+1 implies invariant at next cursor, for ALL arrays, values, lengths and offsets.
Stage completion: invariant at cursor i=L implies every element in [0,L) equals v; this is the precondition for next stage.
Final scan: all written array values equal v ensures read/select(A,n+i)=v for ANY 0≤i<L.
State invariant is satisfiable with arbitrary distinct old and new values (nonvacuity).
Mutating the store to wrong value (v+1) must have a satisfiable counterexample (cannot falsely PASS).
proof_method: Construct generic SMT-LIB2 script with free integer and array parameters and quantified index j; disprove each universal implication by showing its negation UNSAT. Never instantiate a fixed finite number of stages or indexes. Real Z3 must return exactly unsat for every valid lemma and sat for explicit wrong-value mutant.
scope: Proof scheme is mathematical induction on the repeated stage count N, conditional on parser verifying original CHC matches this precise stage machine. Individual source verification 108/108 includes 6 concrete programs. Do NOT infer generic theorem covers arbitrary arrays, arbitrary array programs, or learned neural invention.
cost: Only theorem-generation and SMT proof runtime measured. No 10x total compute claim without baseline comparison on matched hardware and solver rights.
